text:
Sam Tran: Quick question — I bumped my HSA employee contribution to 6% after my salary change last month and HR also applies the employer top-up. Payroll vendor is switching next Friday — will the employer top-up get split across vendors or could that cause a duplicate top-up? 🤔
Riley Chen: cc @Olivia Park on payroll vendor cutover. We didn't list HSA top-up specifics in the last runbook, good catch.
Olivia Park: Hey @Sam, @Riley — short answer: the top-up is calculated and paid by Redwood payroll before we send files to vendors. During cutover we send a final file to the old vendor and an initial file to the new vendor. That shouldn't create duplicate employer top-ups if mapping is correct.
Olivia Park: Longer: employer contributions are tracked on our payroll system (not the vendor). We send deduction/contribution records to whichever vendor owns the active mapping for that pay period. So as long as the mapping key follows the cutover checklist, YTD stays accurate.
Ben Alvarez: We'll want to confirm the deduction code name with the new vendor so their parser doesn't create a new "employer top-up" line item. If they expect a different code, a mismatch could look like a new contribution.
Olivia Park: Exactly. Mapping snippet to include in runbook:
```
employee_id,deduction_code,amount
12345,HSA_EMP_TOPUP,75.00
```
Please ensure new vendor maps `HSA_EMP_TOPUP` to employer_topup rather than a generic employer_contribution field.
Sam Tran: Got it. I already updated my employee contribution % in the payroll portal. Anything I need to do on my end?
Riley Chen: No action from you, @Sam — people-ops will validate post-cutover reports and confirm your YTD employer top-ups reconcile. We'll ping you if anything looks off.
payroll-bot: Payroll vendor migration scheduled: 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC. Affected services: HSA, FSA, Garnishments. See #payroll-alerts for status updates. :construction:
Olivia Park: Follow-up: if anyone sees a duplicate employer top-up on their stub after the switch, open a support ticket to payroll@redwood.com with a screenshot and pay period date. We can reverse or correct on the next payroll run. Also note: employer top-ups are prorated by pay cycles, so a mid-cycle change might not be a full-period top-up.
Ben Alvarez: Finance note — if there's a retro adjustment request we usually process it as an off-cycle correction. That may affect taxes/withholding; payroll will flag tax implications.
Sam Tran: Thanks all, appreciate the clarity! :thumbsup:
